title: BatchNFTMinter mints to arbitrary recipient — including NFTStaker — bypassing any 'who paid for the NFT' tracking; complicates accounting for incentive programs
economicDescription:
`batchMint` accepts arbitrary `recipient` and routes all minted NFTs there. There is no on-chain link between `msg.sender` (who funded the mint) and the recipient (who holds the NFTs). If the recipient is set to `address(NFTStaker)` directly (as opposed to first minting to a user, who then `stake()`s), the NFTs never go through `stake()` and therefore never increment `users[who].amount` — they just sit on NFTStaker's balance with no per-user accounting. NFTStaker.totalStaked is incremented only via `stake()` (line 446-447), so direct ERC1155 transfers to NFTStaker are stuck — the design.md confirms this at lines 326-331 ('Direct ERC1155 transfer of a foreign ID into the contract does not affect totalStaked or any user's balance').

This is documented for foreign IDs but the same is true for the staked ID: minting NFTs directly TO NFTStaker via batchMint(recipient = NFTStaker) bypasses the stake() entrypoint, so the NFTs are stranded in NFTStaker forever (recoverable only via a future rescue fn). This is a nuisance griefing vector — anyone can spend phUSD to mint NFTs straight into NFTStaker, and those NFTs are then permanently stuck.

Moreover, since the nudge in batchMint pays `recipient`, an attacker who batchMints with `recipient = NFTStaker` would (i) waste mint cost, (ii) strand NFTs in NFTStaker, AND (iii) deliver the entire nudge pool TO NFTStaker (where it would also be stranded if nudgePaymentToken != phUSD). Net: a malicious actor can grief the protocol by simultaneously stranding NFTs and nudges, at the cost of mint-payment.
attackScenario:
1. Attacker calls batchMint(count=nudgeSize=5, recipient=NFTStaker_address, paymentAmount=cost(5)).
2. 5 NFTs are minted to NFTStaker — stuck (no user owns them; NFTStaker.totalStaked unchanged).
3. The full nudge pool is transferred to NFTStaker — stuck if nudgePaymentToken != phUSD (no rescue fn in NFTStaker either; but if nudgePaymentToken == phUSD, this would actually inflate the staking budget — but ECON setup forbids paymentToken == nudgePaymentToken; nothing forbids phUSD == nudgePaymentToken when phUSD != paymentToken).
4. Attacker has spent cost(5) phUSD to permanently lock NFTs and the nudge pool.

Net damage: attacker pays a few thousand phUSD to lock tens-of-thousands of USDC and several NFTs. Pure griefing. Profitable only if attacker is adversarial to protocol (e.g. a competitor) and the cost-to-damage ratio is favorable.
profitability: Negative for attacker (purely destructive). Low ratio of attacker-cost to protocol-damage when nudge pool is large.
affectedParties: stakers (slight delay if nudge token == phUSD and got locked rather than enriching the budget — depends on what nudgePaymentToken is)
recommendedMitigation:
- BatchNFTMinter: add an optional `denylist` of recipients (e.g. exclude known-protocol contracts from being recipients).
- Or: require `recipient.code.length == 0` (EOA-only recipients) — too restrictive for legitimate composability.
- Better: in NFTStaker, add an admin `rescueERC20(token, amount, to)` and `rescueERC1155(id, amount, to)` that lets the owner recover stranded balances after the fact. Bound by `totalStaked` for the staked ID so user-deposited NFTs cannot be rescued.
- Better still: have the BatchNFTMinter verify that `recipient.supportsInterface(type(IERC1155Receiver).interfaceId)` is plausible and that `recipient != address(any-staker-contract)` via a configurable blocklist.
intentReference: design.md lines 326-331 acknowledge that direct transfers to NFTStaker for foreign IDs are 'just stuck tokens, recoverable via future rescue if we add one'. The staked-ID variant is symmetric and equally griefable. The known-issues file does not address this for batchMint specifically.
